Grammar and usage (tense, mood, modality and concord, aspects of language use in everyday life). Logical and critical thinking and

courses.title: Nigerian Peoples and Culture
skills_learned: analyse the historical foundation of the Nigerian culture and arts in pre-colonial times
list and identify the major linguistic groups in Nigeria
explain the gradual evolution of Nigeria as a political unit
analyse the concepts of trade, economic and self-reliance status of the Nigerian peoples towards national development
enumerate the challenges of the Nigerian State towards nation building
analyse the role of the judiciary in upholding people's fundamental rights
identify acceptable norms and values of the major ethnic groups in Nigeria; and
list and suggest possible solutions to identifiable Nigerian environmental, moral and value problems
courses.content_summary: Nigerian history, culture, and art up to 1800 (Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo peoples and culture; peoples and culture of the ethnic minority groups). Nigeria under colonial rule (advent of colonial rule in Nigeria; Colonial administration of Nigeria). Evolution of Nigeria as a political unit (amalgamation of Nigeria in 1914, formation of political parties in Nigeria, nationalist movement and struggle for

courses.title: Introduction to Agriculture I
skills_learned: have a broad understanding of the concepts and dimensions of agriculture in modern times with emphasis on Nigeria and the tropics
acquire basic knowledge and understanding of the roles of agriculture and the place of soil, crop and animal resources in the production process as well as the constraints they face
be familiar with the role of technologies in the transformation of agriculture; and
explain potentials and constraints to sustainable agricultural production
courses.content_summary: Meaning and Scope of Agriculture. Importance of Agriculture to an expanded economy. Agricultural Ecology. Genetics, Agronomy. Rocks and Soil formation. Soil and Water Conservation. Soil Fertility. Land Preparation methods (soil tillage systems). Soil-water-plant relationship. Plant Forms and functions, Growth, Development and Reproduction. Plant Propagation Methods. Cropping Systems, Planting Patt

courses.title: Introduction to Agriculture II
skills_learned: explain the history of agricultural development and the role of the public and private sectors
identify and analyse the factors of agricultural production and the role of various resources; and
explain constraints of technology and mechanization, and the role of agricultural extension transformation
courses.content_summary: History of Agricultural Development in West Africa, Roles of Government and NGOs in Agricultural Development, Factors of agricultural production, Basic Economic Principles, Characteristic Features of Agricultural Production, Labour Management, Farm Management, Marketing of Agricultural Produce, Agricultural Extension, Agricultural Technology, Farm surveying and farmstead planning, Simple Farm Tool

courses.title: General Biology I
skills_learned: explain cell structure and organizations
summarize functions of cellular organelles
characterize living organisms and state their general reproduction
describe the interrelationship that exists between organisms
discuss the concept of heredity and evolution; and
enumerate habitat types and their characteristics
courses.content_summary: Cell structure and organization, functions of cellular organelles, characteristics and classification of living things, chromosomes, genes and their relationships and importance, general reproduction, interrelationships of organisms (competitions, parasitism, predation, symbiosis, commensalisms, mutualism, saprophytism); heredity and evolution (introduction to Darwinism and Lamarkism, Mendelian la

courses.title: General Biology Practical I
skills_learned: outline common laboratory hazards
provide precautions on laboratory hazards
state the functions of the different parts of microscope
use the microscope and describe its maintenance
draw biological diagrams and illustrations; and
apply scaling and proportion to biological diagrams
courses.content_summary: Common laboratory hazards: prevention and first aid; measurements in biology; uses and care of microscope: compound and dissecting microscope. Biological drawings and illustration, scaling, accuracy, and proportion; use of common laboratory apparatus and laboratory experiments designed to illustrate the topics covered in BIO 101.

courses.title: General Chemistry I
skills_learned: define atom, molecules and chemical reactions
discuss the Modern electronic theory of atoms
write electronic configurations of elements on the periodic table

Electronic configuration, periodicity and building up of the periodic table. Hybridization and shapes of simple molecules. Valence Forces. Structure of solids. Chemical equations and stoichiometry; Chemical bonding and intermolecular forces, kinetic theory of matter. Elementary thermochemistry. Rate

skills_learned: state the importance and development of organic chemistry
define fullerenes and its applications
discuss electronic theory

discuss comparative chemistry of group 1A, IIA and IVA elements; and
describe basic properties of Transition metals

Electronic theory in organic chemistry. Isolation and purification of organic compounds. Determination of structures of organic compounds including qualitative and quantitative analysis in organic chemistry. Nomenclature and functio

skills_learned: describe the general laboratory rules and safety procedures
collect scientific data and correctly carrying out Chemical experiments
identify the basic glassware and equipment in the laboratory
identify the differences between primary and secondary standards
perform redox titration
recording observations and measurements in the laboratory notebooks; and
analyse the data to arrive at scientific conclusions
courses.content_summary: Laboratory experiments designed to reflect topics presented in courses CHM 101 and CHM 102. These include acid-base titrations, qualitative analysis, redox reactions, gravimetric analysis, data analysis and presentation.

courses.title: General Chemistry Practical II
skills_learned: identify the general laboratory rules and safety procedures
collect scientific data and correctly carrying out Chemical experiments
identify the basic glassware and equipment in the laboratory
identify and carry out preliminary tests which includes ignition, boiling point, melting point, test on known and unknown organic compounds
perform solubility tests on known and unknown organic compounds
conduct elemental tests on known and unknown compounds; and
conduct functional group/confirmatory test on known and unknown compounds which could be acidic / basic / neutral organic compounds
courses.content_summary: Continuation of CHM 107. Additional laboratory experiments to include functional group analysis, quantitative analysis using volumetric methods.

skills_learned: explain basic definition of Set, Subset, Union, Intersection, Complements and use of Venn diagrams
solve quadratic equations
solve trigonometric functions
identify various types of numbers; and
solve some problems using Binomial theorem
courses.content_summary: Elementary set theory, subsets, union, intersection, complements, venn diagrams. Real numbers, integers, rational and irrational numbers. courses.title: Elementary Mathematics II
skills_learned: identify the types of rules in differentiation and integration
describe the meaning of Function of a real variable, graphs, limits and continuity; and
solve some applications of definite integrals in areas and volumes
courses.content_summary: Function of a real variable, graphs, limits and idea of continuity. The derivative, as limit of rate of change. Techniques of differentiation. Extreme curve sketching; Integration as an inverse of differentiation. Methods of integration, Definite integrals. Application to areas, volumes.

courses.title: General Physics II

describe and determine the magnetic field for steady and moving charges

make observations of events, collect and tabulate data

plot and analyse graphs

identify the main branches of philosophy & the centrality of logic in philosophical discourse
know the elementary rules of reasoning
distinguish between valid and invalid arguments
think critically and assess arguments in texts, conversations and day-to-day discussions

courses.title: Entrepreneurship and Innovation
skills_learned: explain the concepts and theories of entrepreneurship, intrapreneurship, opportunity seeking, new value creation, and risk taking
state the characteristics of an entrepreneur
analyse the importance of micro and small businesses in wealth creation, employment, and financial independence
engage in entrepreneurial thinking
identify key elements in innovation
describe stages in enterprise formation, partnership and networking including business planning
describe contemporary entrepreneurial issues in Nigeria, Africa, and the rest of the world; and
state the basic principles of e-commerce
courses.content_summary: Concept of entrepreneurship (Entrepreneurship, Intrapreneurship/Corporate entrepreneurship). Theories, rationale and relevance of entrepreneurship (Schumpeterian and other perspectives, risk-taking, necessity and opportunity-based entrepreneurship and creative destruction). Characteristics of entrepreneurs (opportunity seeker, risk taker, natural and nurtured, problem solver and change agent, inno

courses.title: Introduction to Crop Production
skills_learned: discuss the various systems of crop production in Nigeria
identify various agro-ecological zones in Nigeria; and
explain the best way of managing forest resources for sustainable development
courses.content_summary: Definitions of the terms, crops and plants (including weeds). Importance of crops and plants to mankind. Origin of different types of crops in tropical, sub-tropical and temperate climatic regions and introduction of crop types to other lands. Botany and basis for classification and/or grouping of crops. Descriptions of various types of crops (grains and legumes, cereal crops, root and tuber crops

courses.title: Introduction to Agricultural Economics, Extension and Rural Sociology
skills_learned: explain basic economic theories, construct the supply and demand curves and use these to determine market equilibrium
discuss the basic workings of the economy, national income determination from the output and income perspectives, and the condition for equilibrium of the national economy
define the concepts of international trade and balance of payment
discuss the process of money creation and banking in the national economy
explain the concept of welfare economics
define and make valid comparison on agricultural extension methodologies world over
categorize the major rural social institutions, processes, and the need for social changes in rural communities; and
explain the dynamics of leadership for social changes
courses.content_summary: The nature of economics and economic problems. Scope of agricultural economics and methods. The concept of opportunity cost; supply and demand and their application to agricultural problems. Production functions, cost analysis and functions. Concept of elasticities. Type of markets, perfect competition, monopoly, oligopoly etc. Price theory and some applications. The components of agriculture in n

courses.title: Introduction to Forestry and Wildlife Management
skills_learned: enumerate the potentials of renewable natural resources
identify important forest tree species as well as wildlife species in the various vegetation zones of Nigeria
establish small scale bee farm, snail farm, cane rat farm
elucidate the importance of forestry and wildlife to the national economy; and
raise seedlings of economic tree species
courses.content_summary: Renewable natural resources availability, distribution, and potentials. The important forest trees and wildlife. Organization of forest resources and non-timber resources. Classification, morphology, taxonomy and ecology of tropical forest trees and game reserves in Nigeria. Silviculture, afforestation characteristics of major timbers and their uses. Forest production activities. Forest protection

courses.title: Introduction to Animal Production
skills_learned: Prospects and problems of the animal industry
Identification/description of types of farm animals
Feeds and feeding management of farm animals
Housing and management systems of different livestock
Principles of animal health management
Animal breeding and breed improvement principles; and
Basic anatomy and physiology of the living systems (histology, circulatory, respiratory, digestive, reproductive, etc)
courses.content_summary: The livestock industry – problems and prospects. Description of the breeds of cattle, sheep, goats, pigs, poultry, and rabbits. Systems of livestock production, Feeding and feed management. Principles of breeding and livestock improvement. General principles of management of the different types of farm animals (cattle, sheep, goats, pigs, poultry, and rabbits). Introduction to game and companion a

courses.title: Introduction to Fisheries and Aquaculture
skills_learned: relate with different terminologies with regards to fish and fisheries, aquaculture production systems
situate the importance of fisheries and aquaculture to the Nigerian economy, human nutrition, environment, and sociocultural systems
describe linkages between fisheries and aquaculture
explain the problems and principles of fisheries management and aquaculture
describe the prospects and opportunities in fisheries management and aquaculture to individuals and the country
situate and differentiate the various practices of fisheries management and different aquaculture practices
gain fundamental knowledge underpinning the classification of fisheries and aquaculture by scale (small, medium, and large scales)
understand the fundamentals of fisheries management in relation to overfishing and sustainable development; and
list the types of management tools
courses.content_summary: Concepts of fisheries and aquaculture in relation to natural resources. Water bodies and fisheries and aquaculture practices in Nigeria. Fish adaptation to aquatic life. The important fishes of West Africa with emphasis on Nigeria species. Classification, evolution, morphology, and basic structure of fishes. Life cycle of principal species of fishes. Significance of fishes in the life of Nigerians

courses.title: Principles of Family and Consumer Sciences, Food Science and Technology
skills_learned: state the philosophy and objectives of family and consumer sciences
distinguish between different areas of family and consumer sciences
identify professional opportunities in family and consumer sciences
describe the role of family and consumer sciences professionals in the society
define and explain the scope of Food Science and Technology as a course
describe the methods of distribution and marketing of foods
identify the causes of food poisoning and the ways it could be prevented
state the functions of food, and methods of food processing and preservation; and
describe the composition and structures of Nigerian/West African food
courses.content_summary: Philosophy, scope, objectives and historical development of family and consumer sciences. Examination of basic human needs with respect to food, clothing, shelter, and health. Programme approaches in family and consumer sciences which will help meet these needs. Professional opportunities in family and consumer sciences. The role of a family and consumer sciences professional in today's society. D

courses.title: Introduction to Business
skills_learned: identify business cycle process to establish an enterprise in agribusiness;
identify the functions of business organisations; and
analyse challenges facing business enterprises.
courses.content_summary: Introduction to Business: business definitions, forms of ownership, functions of business organization, and the definition, scope, prospects and challenges of agribusiness.

courses.title: Business Law
skills_learned: provide legal backing to the establishment of business enterprise;
apply legal decision in the running of the Agribusiness enterprise;
familiarise with the various legal sectors and their jurisdictions; and
understand the Conditions governing business transactions with individuals and corporate organisations.
courses.content_summary: Business Law: the Nigerian legal system and court structure, law of contract, agency, sale of goods, tort, hire purchase, employment, insurance, partnership, and negotiable instruments.

courses.title: Principles of Soil Science
skills_learned: the role of the soil as a component of the environment
the various disciplines of Soil and Job opportunities as Soil Scientists
how soils are formed and the need to use the soil sustainably
the various physical, chemical and biological activities taking place in the soil in order to prescribe appropriate management needs
the need to survey, classify and map soil for various purposes
the various challenges facing the soil under different situations; and
relationship between climate change, soil management and utilization
courses.content_summary: Soil as a natural Resource in the Environment; Sub-disciplines of Soil Science and employment opportunities; Soil Genesis/Formation and Development; Factors of Soil Formation. Soil Composition and Soil Ecosystem Functions; Soil Physical, Chemical and Biological properties (Texture, Structure, Density, Soil Solution, Soil Temperature, Soil Reaction, Salinity, Mineralization, Humification; Ammonific

courses.title: Peace and Conflict Resolution
skills_learned: analyse the concepts of peace, conflict, and security
list major forms, types and root causes of conflicts and violence
differentiate between conflict and terrorism; enumerate security and peace building strategies; and
describe roles of international organisations, media, and traditional institutions in peace building
courses.content_summary: Concepts of peace, conflict and security in a multi-ethnic nation. Types and theories of conflicts: ethnic, religious, and economic. Geo-political conflicts; structural conflict theory, realist theory of conflict, frustration-aggression conflict theory. Root causes of conflict and violence in Africa: indigene and settlers' phenomenon. Boundaries/boarder disputes, political disputes, ethnic dispute

courses.title: Venture Creation
skills_learned: describe the key steps in venture creation
spot opportunities in problems and in high potential sectors regardless of geographical location
state how original products, ideas, and concepts are developed
develop business concept for further incubation or pitching for funding
identify key sources of entrepreneurial finance
implement the requirements for establishing and managing micro and small enterprises; conduct entrepreneurial marketing and e-commerce
apply a wide variety of emerging technological solutions to entrepreneurship; and
appreciate why ventures fail due to lack of planning and poor implementation
courses.content_summary: Opportunity identification (sources of business opportunities in Nigeria, environmental scanning, demand and supply gap/unmet needs/market gaps/market research, unutilised resources, social and climate conditions, and technology adoption gap). New business development (business planning, market research). Entrepreneurial finance (venture capital, equity finance, micro finance, personal savings, sm

courses.title: Agribusiness Communication Skills
skills_learned: explain the essence of value addition to business enterprise
verify the different methodological approach to value chain analysis of commodities
identify the various stakeholders in the value chain
estimate value added at each stage of chain; and
integrate commodities along the chain

courses.title: Quantitative Analysis
skills_learned: possess the ability to collate reliable data from different sources;
handle and manipulate quantitative data;
apply different analytical fitted techniques to analyse data; and
compute and interpret data for meaningful decision.
courses.content_summary: Quantitative Analysis: quantitative tools (probabilities, matrices, calculus), business decision theory, sensitivity analysis, correlation and regression, operational research and linear programming.

courses.title: Agribusiness Marketing and Cooperative
skills_learned: provide legal backing to the establishment of business enterprise
apply legal decision in the running of the Agribusiness enterprise
familiarise with the various legal sectors and their jurisdictions; and
understand the Conditions governing business transactions with individuals and corporate organisations

courses.title: Food and Agribusiness Marketing
skills_learned: identify the various theory personality developer and describe their key characteristics.
apply relevant theory models to the current Nigerian situation of Agribusiness management.
identify bad business practices and behaviours that may harm business smooth development and sustainability.
courses.content_summary: Agribusiness Management Theory and Practice: levels and features of management theory, classical to modern management theories, and their application to the Nigerian socio-cultural context.

courses.title: Farm Business Management and Production Economics
skills_learned: technically organise factors of production
mix factors of production appropriately for profit making
understand the application of management techniques for optimal production; and
perform planning and budgeting of business enterprise to suit current realities

courses.title: Agribusiness Information Management
skills_learned: technically organise factors of production;
mix factors of production appropriately for profit making;
understand the application of management techniques for optimal production; and
perform planning and budgeting of business enterprise to suit current realities.
courses.content_summary: Farm Business Management and Production Economics: production function estimation, cost/revenue analysis, factor-factor/factor-product/product-product relationships, risk management, budgeting and linear programming in farm planning.

courses.title: Introduction to Application of Computer in Agribusiness
skills_learned: explain basic information technology terms
use the computer and software packages to create databases; and
store information and analyze it using common software such as the Microsoft Excel and Access, SPSS, SAS, R statistics, E Views etc

courses.title: Research Method and Statistics
skills_learned: investigate a research problem related to agribusiness enterprise;
identify and demonstrate facility in research designs and data collection strategies that are most appropriate to Agribusiness research project; and
develop effective writing skills.
courses.content_summary: Research Methods and Statistics: principles of research design, variables and data types, questionnaire design, inferential statistics, sampling, hypothesis testing, and scientific report writing.

courses.title: Entrepreneurship and Agribusiness Development
skills_learned: identify the nature and characteristics of business organisations
compare and contrast Agribusiness forms of organisations and explain their advantages and disadvantages; and
develop a business idea worth of investing as an expert

courses.title: Financial Management and Policy I & II
skills_learned: distinguish sources of finance' advantages and disadvantages to business enterprises;
practice prudent management of financial capital;
use methodological approach to financial investment evaluation; and
acquire the knowledge of the measurement of the healthy position of a business investment.
courses.content_summary: Financial Management and Policy: time value of money, sources of finance, capital structure, leverage, cost of capital, working capital management, financial ratios, and capital budgeting (NPV, IRR).

courses.title: Econometrics for Agribusiness
skills_learned: source for and handle secondary data;
effectively handle quantitative data analysis for Agribusiness investment;
have the capacity to manage and use various and relevant Econometric software; and
undertake and interpret analysed data.
courses.content_summary: Econometrics for Agribusiness: classical linear regression model, OLS, multiple regression, dummy variables, violations of CLRM assumptions, and applications to agribusiness production, consumption and demand analysis.

courses.title: Agribusiness Investment and Project Analysis
skills_learned: describe different types of project investment in Agribusiness;
identify types of financial valuation techniques and measurements; and
evaluate Agribusiness investments using acceptable procedures.
courses.content_summary: Agribusiness Investment and Project Analysis: project evaluation techniques (NPV, IRR, payback), cash flow and tax effects, feasibility/technical/economic/financial/sensitivity analysis, and security valuation models.

courses.title: Export Management and International Business
skills_learned: manage agribusiness enterprises to reflect international standards;
identify export commodities and their comparative economic advantage; and
develop international skills that will enable them interact with multinational markets and logistics.
courses.content_summary: Export Management and International Business: export management skills, logistics and freight, free trade zones, globalization, INCO terms and documentation, and control and management of MNCs.

courses.title: Seminar in Agribusiness Management
skills_learned: select suitable researchable topics of study;
search for and analyse related literatures in selected areas of the chosen topics; and
develop and demonstrate proficiency in writing and verbal skills.
courses.content_summary: Seminar in Agribusiness: writing and presenting a research proposal covering problem statement, objectives, literature review and methodology (statistical/econometric tools).

courses.title: Research Project
skills_learned: identify an investigative research problem;
employ data collection instruments, measures, processes to solve problems in Agribusiness; and
conduct independent research with minimal supervision.
